claims.text: Ti/Zr hydride precursors should be decomposed below 400 °C because rapid oxygen diffusion into the metal lattice begins above this range.
Hydride decomposition and extrusion require vacuum or an ultra-high-purity inert atmosphere containing less than 1 ppm O2.
Maintaining oxygen partial pressure below 10^-6 Pa throughout decomposition and sintering prevents brittle alpha-HCP oxide formation.
Maintaining oxygen partial pressure below 10^-6 Pa prevents formation of Al-Zr/Ti intermetallics.
A ramp of 1-5 °C/min to 350-400 °C ensures complete hydride decomposition and hydrogen outgassing.
Slow heating during hydride decomposition prevents hydrogen-pressure gradients that cause cracking.
Rapid heating to an extrusion temperature of 1000-1200 °C promotes dynamic recrystallization and grain refinement.
Solid-solution HEA formation is favored by atomic-size difference δ ≤ 6.6% and mixing enthalpy -11.6 < ΔHmix < 3.2 kJ mol−1.
Satisfying the stated δ and ΔHmix criteria prevents brittle intermetallic formation.
A fine-grained BCC matrix containing 10-20% metastable B2 or Laves phases provides precipitation strengthening.
A 10-20% fraction of metastable B2 or Laves phases can strengthen the alloy without compromising its brittle-to-ductile transition.
Reducing final grain size below 5 μm improves strength and creep resistance through the Hall-Petch effect.
Group IV alloying can induce a brittle-to-ductile transition in BCC refractory alloys through electronic-structure changes and Jahn-Teller distortions.
The proposed process will produce a bulk RHEA with greater than 98% relative density.
The processed alloy will have room-temperature yield strength greater than 800 MPa.
The processed alloy will retain yield strength greater than 400 MPa at 1000 °C.
The processed alloy will exhibit greater than 10% room-temperature compressive strain.
The proposed thermal and atmospheric controls will prevent catastrophic cracking during processing.
The final microstructure will be predominantly BCC and contain less than 5% metastable B2 precipitates.
Alloys containing more than 15 at% Al may form excessive brittle intermetallics even when oxygen is controlled.

contradictions.description: The target metastable-phase fraction is stated as 10-20%, while the predicted final microstructure is specified to contain less than 5% B2 precipitates.

Ultra-pure argon with less than 1 ppm O2 is offered as an alternative to vacuum, but at ordinary argon pressure this does not satisfy the separately asserted oxygen partial-pressure limit of less than 10^-6 Pa.

The hypothesis predicts that air and rapid heating promote catastrophic cracking, but the falsification rule says catastrophic cracking in the air/rapid-ramp sample would falsify the claimed necessity of vacuum and slow heating; that result would instead support the directional prediction.
